x: In the high hurdles Neil Owen showed impressive form in the A race to finish second while new member Dominic Girdler got his Belgrave career off to an exciting start with a fine win in the B event.
In the short hurdles Neil Owen was close to beating Commonwealth bound Damian Greaves while Dominic Girdler ensured more good points with a B win.

Goldie Sayers placed 11th in the Javelin, not so far behind her season's best, but Scot Thompson was out of sorts as he was only able to manage 48.89 in the discus, some 7 metres down on his best for the year. Dominic Girdler had an injury problem and was unable to compete in the sprint hurdles.

In the European U23 Championships, we were represented by Tim Abeyie (gold 4x100 m), Tim Benjamin (silver 400 m), Darren Chin (gold 4 x 100 m), Dominic Girdler, Chris Lambert (gold 200 m and 4 x 100 m), Samson Oni, Goldie Sayers and Scot Thompson.
Dominic Girdler finished a brilliant second to Damien Grieves but had the satisfaction of gaining Chris Baillie's scalp by the narrowest of margins.
New member Dan Donovan made an impressive start while under 23 year olds Scot Thompson, Greg Beard, Seni Majekodunmi, and Dominic Girdler made significant contributions.

By coincidence Dominic Girdler ran the same time as Matt to get second in the B race. The 800m didn’t go to plan and Graeme Oudney could not explain why he was 7 seconds down on his season’s best as he trailed in last in the A race.
A glimmer of hope was provided when William Sharman squeezed a sprint hurdles victory into a huge headwind followed by a clear second victory from Dominic Girdler in the B event.
Dominic Girdler accepted one match, competing in Hungary on Friday evening, but then got up at 3am to catch the red eye back to Luton, followed by a train to Loughborough and car to Birmingham.
